export.title: AlgoSentinel — autonomous complexity-regression agent
export.model: Cursor Agent (build) + gemini-2.5-flash (runtime agent under test)
export.author: G Karthik Koundinya

messages.content:
ok so for this take-home i want to build an agent that reviews github PRs for complexity regressions. like when a function goes from O(n) to O(n^2), tests still pass but it blows up at scale. domain is repo automation. python 3.11, gemini for the model, docker for running code.

hard requirements i have to hit:
- 50+ tools, 4+ namespaces, and the MODEL picks the tools (no hand-written if/else routing)
- one tool that spawns a real subagent in its own isolated context with its own tools
- a single run that does 20+ tool calls and doesn't lose the plan
- production stuff: logging, retries w/ backoff, rate limiting, typed errors, eval harness, unit + integration tests
- at least one tool that takes another tool's output as input

let's nail the architecture first before we write anything.

Here's the shape I'd go with:

- 4 namespaces: github (PR/diff/review I/O), sandbox (Docker run + profiling), complexity (curve fit, class inference, regression detect), optimizer (fix gen, review body, summary).
- A ToolRegistry keyed by `namespace__tool`. Each tool registers with a Pydantic input model and the Gemini schema is derived from it. Dispatch is a dict lookup so tool #55 doesn't become an if-chain.
- AgentLoop (parent) selects over all tools. FunctionAnalysisSubagent gets its own client + message history, scoped to sandbox + complexity only, returns a typed ComplexityReport.
- ContextManager pins the plan in the system prompt and compresses tool history every few calls.
- Composition: profile_runtime → fit_complexity_curves → infer_complexity_class → detect_regression → generate_pr_review_body.

Want me to scaffold the registry + resilience + observability first?

yeah do the foundation first. typed errors (retryable vs fatal split), tenacity retry with exp backoff + jitter, a token bucket rate limiter for the model calls, structlog json logs, and the registry. and keep dispatch a dict lookup, not a switch.

Foundation done. errors.py has RetryableError/FatalError + per-subsystem subclasses; with_retry only retries RetryableError. TokenBucketRateLimiter caps model calls/min. structlog json configured. ToolRegistry builds the Gemini FunctionDeclarations from each tool's Pydantic model and dispatches by name. Added unit tests for registry, retry, rate limiter — green.

now github + sandbox namespaces. github: pr details, diff, list files, file content at a ref, commit diff, post review/comment, branch+push+create pr for the fix flow, and the subagent spawn tool. sandbox: create/destroy docker sandbox, execute fn, install deps, run tests, logs/health, gen inputs, extract function, profile runtime, profile memory, benchmark pair, validate correctness. profiling needs to time across input sizes so we can fit a curve after.

18 github tools + 14 sandbox tools done (32/55). profile_runtime runs the fn in a throwaway docker container across input sizes [10..10000] and returns timing points. extract_function pulls a named fn out of a file with AST so the subagent can profile it standalone. sandbox integration tests pass against docker.

complexity namespace + the subagent now. the subagent is the part they'll actually scrutinize so make it a real isolated agent, not a function pretending to be one. own client, own message history, scoped to sandbox+complexity, drives its own loop: profile pre+post, fit curves, infer classes, detect regression, classify severity, return a ComplexityReport. also add the ContextManager so the parent doesn't lose the plan on long runs.

13 complexity tools added (scipy curve fit, R^2, class inference, order-based regression detect, severity) → 45/55. FunctionAnalysisSubagent runs its own gemini loop with declarations scoped via SUBAGENT_NAMESPACES = ['sandbox','complexity'], keeps its own _messages, returns a validated ComplexityReport. ContextManager pins the plan and compresses tool history every 6 calls. Added an integration test asserting the subagent's tool set is a strict subset of the parent's and its history is independent.

finish optimizer + the parent AgentLoop + fastapi webhook + cli. then the eval harness with golden cases. make sure one run actually crosses 20 tool calls. composition should just happen since the subagent feeds profiler output through the complexity chain.

10 optimizer tools added → 55/55. AgentLoop does the whole audit: fetch PR → diff → spawn subagent per changed fn → collect reports → review → post. FastAPI /webhook/github fires audits on PR events; /health asserts tool_count >= 55. CLI is scripts/run_agent.py. Eval harness scores precision/recall/F1 on golden cases. Pipeline test confirms a single session crosses 20 tool calls (parent + subagent) with the plan intact.

let's actually run the real gemini agent against a live PR end to end. i want to see the parent pick tools and the subagent run in its own context, then post the review. set up a demo PR with an O(n) -> O(n^2) regression.

Live run died instantly: 429 with `limit: 0` on gemini-2.0-flash. That's not quota — limit:0 looks like a dead model. Checked Google's deprecation page and yep, gemini-2.0-flash was shut down on 2026-06-01, right in the middle of the window. Listed the models the key can reach and smoke-tested them — gemini-2.5-flash, 2.5-flash-lite and 3.5-flash all respond. Switching the default to gemini-2.5-flash.

args.command: python -c "from google import genai; [print(m.name) for m in genai.Client().models.list()]"

messages.content: nice catch. rerun on 2.5-flash and let's see how far it gets.

On 2.5-flash it runs for real. Parent called get_pr_details → get_pr_diff → list_pr_files → get_file_content → extract_function → spawn_function_analysis_subagent, and the subagent ran its own chain create_sandbox → profile_runtime ×2 → fit_complexity_curves ×2 → infer_complexity_class in isolation. Then it hit the free-tier ceiling (this key is 5/min and 20/day per model). Two real issues showed up under load: parent and each subagent were each building their own rate limiter, and on flash-lite the model's thinking tokens ate the output budget and sometimes returned a candidate with no parts, which crashed the loop.

fix both properly. rate limiting should be per api key not per component. and the loop can't crash on an empty response. also a per-day quota 429 — don't retry into it, that's pointless, just fail clearly.

Done. Made the rate limiter a process-wide shared bucket the parent + every subagent draw from, and capped the burst so a full bucket can't trip the rolling per-minute limit on the first tick. Disabled model thinking via a configurable budget for clean tool-calling. Guarded the loop against empty content/parts and nudge it to continue. Added QuotaExhaustedError (fatal) so per-day 429s fail fast instead of burning the rest of the daily allowance. Unit tests green, eval F1 still 1.00.
since a full live run won't fit in 20 req/day on free tier, give me a way to run the same audit with no model calls so i can always demo it.

scripts/full_audit.py runs the identical pipeline deterministically — fetch PR, profile pre/post in docker, run the complexity chain, build the review body, post it — zero model round-trips. It posts a real review on the demo PR. run_agent.py stays the headline gemini path; full_audit.py is the quota-proof equivalent for CI/demos. Updated README + MEMO with the model migration and the free-tier reality.
last check — confirm the 5 required properties hold against the actual code and the tool count + namespaces are right.

Checked against the live registry: 55 tools — github 18, sandbox 14, complexity 13, optimizer 10. Subagent scoped to ['sandbox','complexity']. (1) 55 tools / 4 namespaces, dict dispatch, schema-derived selection. (2) Real subagent: own client + history, scoped tools, typed ComplexityReport — seen live in the traces. (3) Long-horizon: single session > 20 tool calls with the plan pinned; pipeline test asserts it. (4) Scaffolding: structlog, tenacity backoff, shared rate limiter, typed errors, eval harness, unit + integration tests. (5) Composition: profiler output runs through the complexity chain into the review body. All there and exercised.
